Guardian politics live (Andrew Sparrow) — court backlog post filed ~14:30 BST, Thursday 24 September 2026.
Primary source: Ministry of Justice, Criminal court statistics quarterly, April to June 2026, published 24 September 2026 — https://www.gov.uk/government/statistics/criminal-court-statistics-quarterly-april-to-june-2026/criminal-court-statistics-quarterly-april-to-june-2026

HEADLINE: Crown and magistrates' court backlogs in England and Wales hit record highs.

FACTS (Guardian citing MoJ figures):
- 80,829 cases waiting to be heard at crown courts at the end of June — a record since the MoJ began compiling the figures, and 3% up on the previous year.
- Median waiting time from referral to crown court to case completion is 203 days, also a record, up 21% on the previous year.
- 380,230 cases waiting at magistrates' courts at the end of June, up 9% on the previous year.
- Law Society: 23,706 crown court cases have been in the backlog for more than a year — 22% more than a year ago.

QUOTES:
Sarah Sackman, courts minister (Guardian): the figures showed "the scale of the challenge facing our courts, with victims waiting far too long for justice – that's why it's our priority to reduce the backlog so that cases are heard sooner".
Nick Timothy, shadow justice secretary (Guardian): "Labour have spent their time in office attacking our ancient right to a jury trial, rather than taking effective action to tackle the courts crisis." / "With both the crown court and magistrates' court now facing record backlogs, Labour's proposals to simply shift the problem from one part of the court system to another are dead in the water."
Mark Evans, president of the Law Society of England and Wales (Guardian): "The government must seize the chance to deliver a long-term, whole-system plan for criminal justice reform. This should include usable courts, enough judges and staff and the maximum number of sitting days to hear cases promptly."
Alex Norris, Justice Secretary, to Sky News 10:20 BST: "In 2010 there were 29,000 magistrates. The Tory government let that fall to as low as 12,000 - we've got that up to 15,500. But through our campaign we want to get to 21,000 magistrates." On scrapping jury trials: "people have raised really important concerns about this... We are looking at that again. And when we bring back the bill in October, that will reflect those things that we've heard." (Sky News live blog: https://news.sky.com/story/politics-latest-burnham-un-speech-new-york-trump-chagos-12593360)

SECOND SOURCE: Sky News politics live blog, 10:20 BST, confirms the backlog hit a record high and Norris's remarks.
